independence: Each role was filled by separate fresh claude-opus-5-5 sessions (subject x3, safety x2, language x2, lessons split by count), each given only its own role's work orders (openlessons jury orders) and told never to open another role's orders or verdicts; verdicts were written to per-role folders and combined only by jury run after all seven sessions had finished. The drafting model (claude-fable-5) sat on no role.

claims.claim: Young pupils learn to keep personal information private online and to go to a trusted adult for help when content or contact worries them.

sources.title: National curriculum in England: computing programmes of study

notes: safe-advice: the teach text 'لا نعطيها لشخص لا نعرفه' (we do not give it to someone we do not know) implies private information may be given to anyone the child knows, including online 'friends' they feel they know; it should say private information is shared only with a trusted adult's permission.

safe-advice: the example 'لوني المفضل ليس سرا' frames private information as a 'secret' (سر); safety teaching for this age separates private information from secrets, because secrets kept from adults are a grooming signal. Use 'خاص' (private) consistently.
safe-advice: the teach text never states the objective's key safety step (tell a trusted adult when something online worries you); it appears only as reteach 'if unsure'.

The lesson teaches 'خاصة' (private) but the example switches to 'سرا' (secret), mixing two ideas (and 'secret' is a word children are taught not to keep from parents). Corrected example: 'لوني المفضل ليس معلومة خاصة'.
